item.title: When a list lapses
item.description:
A revocation check that lets everything through when the list cannot be had is the one an attacker who can block the list defeats. So when authn-revokd holds no current list from a source, what that source’s list protects isrefused, until a current list arrives again.

output while a source has no current list
a KRL, for sshd authn-revokd writes a KRL that revokes the source’s CA key
a CRL, for a TLS server the expired CRL is left in place; OpenSSL refuses an expired CRL by itself

For sshd: revoking the CA itself

sshd has no notion of a list’s expiry: it would go on reading the last file written for ever. But it checks the CA key of every certificate againstRevokedKeys. So, in place of the list it cannot vouch for, authn-revokd puts the CA’s own key into the output, and every certificate that CA signed is refused, and nothing else.

Here the issuer is stopped, and the KRL source has max_age = "30s", so the copy held lapses within a minute instead of an hour. The CRL source has nomax_age, and its copy is still current:

$ authn-revokd -config revokd-maxage.hcl -once
bridge-ssh: revocation: Get "http://127.0.0.1:28473/ssh/krl": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:28473: connect: connection refused
bridge-x509: revocation: Get "http://127.0.0.1:28473/x509/crl": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:28473: connect: connection refused
output sshd: wrote /tmp/authn/revokd/out/sshd.krl
authn-revokd: not current: bridge-ssh; not fetched: bridge-x509 (the list held is current until 2026-10-26T12:27:10Z)
$ ssh-keygen -Q -l -f out/sshd.krl
# KRL version 0
# Generated at 19700101T010000
# Comment: authn-revokd sshd: FAIL CLOSED, every certificate refused from bridge-ssh
hash: SHA256:AnDb/hVURvKYmNr3UBTfpWL0OVGHgKRMbSFicCNn/O4 # ssh-ed25519
$ ssh-keygen -Q -f out/sshd.krl ca-ssh.pub
ca-ssh.pub (go-authn/bridge SSH CA): REVOKED

bridge-ssh is not current, and its output is failed closed; bridge-x509 is only not fetched, and its CRL is left as it was(what -once reports).SHA256:AnDb/... is the bridge’s SSH CA. A certificate it signed is now revoked as far as anything reading the file is concerned. The commands above ran in the revokd directory, where out/ is; this one runs beside it, in the directory that holds the test certificates, as onsshcert-authorize’s page, so the same file is ../revokd/out/sshd.krl:

$ ssh-keygen -Q -f ../revokd/out/sshd.krl alice-cert.pub
alice-cert.pub (alice): REVOKED

The comment says FAIL CLOSED and names the source, so a person readingssh-keygen -Q -l sees why. The file’s date is 1970 when every source has lapsed. The output is written as soon as a sync notices, which for the daemon is its next refresh and for the timer its next tick. When a current list arrives again, the next sync writes it in place of the CA’s key, and the CA’s certificates are accepted again.

The same happens before the first list: a source never fetched has nothing current, and its CA is revoked from the first write. A new installation refuses the CA’s certificates until its first list verifies, rather than accepting them unchecked.

Each CA for itself

In an output that merges several sources, only the lapsed source’s CA is revoked. The others keep their lists. A list that cannot be merged (past the serial ranges go-authn/krl keeps) fails closed for its own CA only, and/healthz names it. Only if the lists merge alone but not together is every CA of the output revoked, and the comment says so(FAIL CLOSED, the output could not be rendered). Keeping the old file instead would let a later lapse go unseen.

For a TLS server: the CRL itself

A CRL already says when it stops being current, and OpenSSL refuses one past its nextUpdate (“CRL has expired”). So authn-revokd leaves the last verified CRL in place, and the TLS server fails closed by itself. That is also whymax_age is refused on a source that feeds a CRL output: a server that loaded the CRL keeps it until its nextUpdate, whatever authn-revokd writes.

Readers that check the expiry themselves

The merged KRL carries an expiry, the first of its current inputs’. A reader that checks it, such as go-fileshare’s ssh_krl_file orsshcert-authorize --krl,sees authn-revokd stop as it would see the issuer stop.

This only works while authn-revokd runs

The file is failed closed by authn-revokd. While it is stopped, sshd keeps reading the last file written, current or not. Hence Restart=always on the daemon, and monitoring the unit, or the timer, or /healthz.
